chunks: 1128 - Zayd al-Shahham narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said:

"O Zayd, interact with the people through their morals. Perform salat in their mosques, visit their sick, and attend their funerals. If you are able to be the Imams and the mu'adhdhins, then do so. For when you do that, they will say: These are the Ja'fariyyah; may Allah have mercy on Ja'far, how excellent is the way he disciplines his companions. But if you abandon that, they will say: These are the Ja'fariyyah; may Allah do to Ja'far [what is deserved], how evil is the way he disciplines his companions."

key_terms.أَخْلَاقِهِمْ: Their manners and social conventions in interpersonal conduct
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةَ: Those who lead the congregational salat
key_terms.الْجَعْفَرِيَّةُ: The followers associated with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمُؤَذِّنِينَ: Those who call the adhan for prayer
key_terms.جَنَائِزَهُمْ: Their funerals, referring to attending funeral rites
key_terms.خَالِقُوا: Deal and associate with others in a courteous and fitting manner
key_terms.مَرْضَاهُمْ: Their sick people, referring to visiting the ill
key_terms.مَسَاجِدِهِمْ: Their mosques, indicating participation in communal worship spaces

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام instruct his followers to interact with other Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs the followers of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام to embody noble character in their dealings with others and to participate positively in shared communal religious life. It emphasizes that the conduct of the Shi'a reflects upon the Imam عليه السلام himself, making good manners, social solidarity, and visible righteousness a religious responsibility.
